scope: Proposition 7.7 (Flow availability under selected laws) of the manuscript “Spectral convergence for critical FK–Ising planar maps” (preprints/Spectral-convergence-for-critical-FK-Ising-planar-maps-October-5-2026/spectral-convergence-critical-fk-ising-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eeb5895c7058765f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix ζ > 0, a tested chronological window, and an open planar confinement U with the preceding fixed-window and positive- clearance cutoffs. In the preceding definition of availability take D = Dm and take dm, ℓm to be the integer-rounded values in (7.9). Let Dm → ∞ be deterministic and below the preselection depth bound, with any finite-view cutoffs slowed below it. Under (7.2), there is no sequence of selected laws supported on hb unavailable times, pairwise separated by ℓm, in an interval of length at most Crm(N), in either of these fixed parameter regimes: (i) 1 < a0 < a < b, with a − 1 sufficiently small relative to (ϑ − 1)(b − a) and hb sufficiently large as in [31, Proposition 10.18]; (ii) 1 < a0 < a ≤ 2, b = B from Lemma 7.5, and hb = 1. The same statement holds for every fixed multiple of the interval length and every fixed positive confinement clearance.
